messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene using these established facts as fixed continuity. Lena is an adult who works at a clinic and lives alone. Marcus is Lena’s brother and is visiting her apartment tonight. Lena has not moved, changed jobs, or adopted any pets. Her apartment is a second-floor unit. Begin with them already inside the apartment. Keep these facts unchanged. Output only story prose.

Marcus stepped around the stack of unopened mail on the counter and dropped his keys beside Lena’s bowl.

“You still get mail like a person who owns a filing cabinet?” he asked.

“I’m choosing to experience it later.”

“That sounds healthy.”

Lena opened the refrigerator. “You want anything?”

“Whatever you’re having.”

“I haven't decided what I’m having.”

“Then I want whatever you decide not to make.”

She looked over her shoulder. “That might be the most accurate description of your relationship with cooking.”

Marcus smiled and sat at the small kitchen table. He glanced toward the window. From the second-floor apartment, the streetlights showed between the buildings below.

“Work bad?” he asked.

“Long.”

“That’s your new answer for everything.”

“It covers a lot.”

She pulled a container of leftovers from the refrigerator and set it on the counter.

“What is that?”

“Pasta.”

“It doesn't look like pasta.”

“It was pasta yesterday.”

Marcus nodded solemnly. “Important distinction.”

Lena laughed and put two plates on the counter.

“I’m still waiting for you to get a dog,” he said.

“You've been waiting for that since I moved in.”

“And you still haven't.”

“I work too much.”

“Exactly. That's why you need a dog.”

“That logic is terrible.”

“It sounds convincing when I say it confidently.”

She carried the plates to the table. “You should try that on your wife.”

“She knows better.”
